messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a spike of fncall validation failures in prod. Validator flags an unexpected "attachments" array on tool responses; used to be object-only. Example payload we got:

maria: ```json
{
  "tool_name": "payments_lookup",
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "attachments": [ { "id": "r1", "meta": {} } ]
  }
}
```

maria: Validator currently rejects this as schema mismatch and we get a hard fncall reject (counts toward reject quota).

dinesh: Are these from a single model version / variant?

maria: Mostly from v3.2.1 canary + some customer traffic routed to compat variant. Pattern: model emits attachments when it references external docs.

kevin: Noted. Two quick questions — 1) Is this happening before or after our adapter layer? 2) Are requests causing retries / double billing when client SDKs get rejects?

anna: We log adapter ingress + validation outcome. Looks like adapter accepts the raw tool output then validation triggers a reject downstream. No automatic retry from service, but some client SDKs do exponential retry on non-200 which can cause duplicate tool calls.

sasha: So there are three levers: adapt/coerce the attachments into the expected object shape, soft-reject (allow through + mark a tag), or keep strict reject and route to degen model variant.

maria: For immediate mitigation I propose: 1) soft-accept attachments for 24h (coerce to object with attachments_meta field) 2) emit a new telemetry tag fncall.attachment_array=true + reason in rejections 3) add console dash tile for this metric and an alert at rate > 0.5% of fncalls

kevin: I worry about silently coercing — could hide real contract bugs. But hard rejects are breaking customers. Maybe soft-accept but tag and surface prominently in Console + send a one-time email to customers who hit it?

dinesh: Agreed on visibility. Implementation plan: adapter-level soft-coerce toggle behind a feature flag. Default off, flip for one region (canary) then full rollout if no downstream regressions. Telemetry must include: original_shape, coerced_shape, model_version, route_id, customer_id (hashed).

anna: We'll need sampling for pii-sensitive fields. We can hash/omit customer_id at ingest, but need enough cardinality to group.

maria: Also: billing/quotas - current reject path counts toward quota differently. If we soft-accept, we should ensure billing reflects actual tool use once accepted. Need finance sign-off if this reduces billed rejections.

kevin: Ok. Action items:
- @dinesh to add adapter flag + coercion code (canary region)
- @anna to add telemetry tags + samplebackfill plan
- @sasha to mock dashboard wireframe for fncall attachment anomalies
- @maria to draft customer comms template

sasha: Dashboard idea: single-time-series percent_of_fncall_rejects_with_attachments, top 10 model_versions, top 10 routes, chart of retries after rejects. Add link to runbook for toggling soft-coerce.
deploy-bot: deploy started: adapter-coerce-flag v1 -> canary (hosts: 2/6)

maria: tests to add: unit test for coercion, e2e with sample tool that emits attachments, and a regression test ensuring we still reject truly malformed shapes (arrays of mixed types).

dinesh: I'll push PR today with the flag. Will include telemetry schema change as discussed. If anyone objects to soft-accept in canary, speak now.

kevin: Fine with canary if telemetry + dashboard ready. Also add a console annotation explaining that soft-accept is temporary and may revert to strict validation at any time.

anna: I'll create a console tile and an alert rule (threshold 0.5% over 5m) and put it in the fncall -> validation dashboard. Will add a log sampling pipeline for failed originals for 10k events/day cap.

maria: Thanks. After canary (24–48h) we'll review telemetry. If attachments are stable and no client regressions, plan for 2-week permissive rollout and SDK update to officially support attachments in schema.

sasha: Also recommend we add a UX affordance in rollouts: when we enable soft-coerce, Console shows a banner on affected routes + link to the runbook.
deploy-bot: canary deployment success on 2/2 hosts.

maria: Great — I'll start customer comms draft and open a support triage channel. If we see retries spike, we'll pause and revert the flag.

kevin: One more: open a billing ticket to ensure we don't double-bill customers during the transition (annotations on invoice).

maria: Filed BILL-4321 and linked in PR. Will follow up after canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
